headline: Schwarber powers Phillies past Jays in 12th, 7-6
recap: The Phillies beat the Toronto Blue Jays 7-6 in 12 innings on Sunday at Citizens Bank Park. Kyle Schwarber hit two home runs and drove in four runs, and starter Jesus Luzardo struck out 12 over seven innings while allowing two runs. Philadelphia built a 5-2 lead through six innings, but Orion Kerkering allowed three runs in the eighth that let Toronto tie it at 5-5. The Blue Jays went back ahead 6-5 in the top of the 12th on a run-scoring double play, but Bryson Stott's RBI single tied it in the bottom half and Derek Hill's walk-off single scored J.T. Realmuto for the win.
The win left Philadelphia at 63-56, second in the NL East, 8.5 games behind the division-leading Atlanta Braves, with a one-game winning streak.

The Phillies open a three-game series at the St. Louis Cardinals today, Monday, first pitch 7:45 PM ET at Busch Stadium. Andrew Painter starts for Philadelphia against Cardinals right-hander Hunter Dobbins. DraftKings has the Phillies as slight favorites at -102.
